column1:
The July 28, 2021 FOMC statement keeps policy highly accommodative—rates at 0–0.25% and asset purchases ongoing—until maximum employment is reached and inflation runs moderately above 2% for some time. Beige Book insights around this date point to broadening momentum: districts reported increased hiring and rising wages, and tourism picked up (notably in the New York District), consistent with the FOMC’s note that the most adversely affected sectors are improving though not fully recovered. Complementing this, the July 2021 SLOOS showed easing bank lending standards and stronger loan demand across businesses and households, indicating credit supply and demand are aligned to support growth. While inflation pressures and virus risks persist, the Beige Book and SLOOS together tilt the outlook more positively than the FOMC statement alone. Therefore, sentiment is revised modestly higher to reflect stronger real‑economy and credit signals.
